items.claimedValue: The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus. It is what makes an element that element.
items.retrievedValue: An element's atomic number is equal to the number of protons in the nuclei of any of its atoms.
items.evidence: An element's atomic number is equal to the number of protons in the nuclei of any of its atoms.
items.verifier: Claude Code subagents (claude-opus-5-5): 1 drafter, 3 independent verifiers; prototype run

items.claimedValue: A neutral atom has the same number of electrons as protons.
items.retrievedValue: Atoms are neutral in electrical charge because they have the same number of negative electrons as positive protons
items.evidence: Atoms are neutral in electrical charge because they have the same number of negative electrons as positive protons
items.verifier: Claude Code subagents (claude-opus-5-5): 1 drafter, 3 independent verifiers; prototype run

items.claimedValue: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
items.retrievedValue: Atoms of the same element that differ in their numbers of neutrons are called isotopes
items.evidence: Atoms of the same element that differ in their numbers of neutrons are called isotopes
items.verifier: Claude Code subagents (claude-opus-5-5): 1 drafter, 3 independent verifiers; prototype run

items.claimedValue: The mass number counts protons and neutrons together, so neutrons = mass number − atomic number.
items.retrievedValue: To find the number of neutrons, subtract the number of protons from the mass number.
items.evidence: To find the number of neutrons, subtract the number of protons from the mass number.
items.verifier: Claude Code subagents (claude-opus-5-5): 1 drafter, 3 independent verifiers; prototype run

items.claimedValue: Orbitals that have the same principal quantum number form a shell, and each shell is divided into subshells.
items.retrievedValue: Orbitals that have the same value of the principal quantum number form a shell . Orbitals within a shell are divided into subshells
items.evidence: Orbitals that have the same value of the principal quantum number form a shell . Orbitals within a shell are divided into subshells
items.verifier: Claude Code subagents (claude-opus-5-5): 1 drafter, 3 independent verifiers; prototype run

items.claimedValue: Valence electrons are the electrons in the highest-numbered shell, plus any in the last unfilled subshell. They largely control an atom's chemistry.
items.retrievedValue: The electrons in the highest-numbered shell, plus any electrons in the last unfilled subshell, are called valence electrons
items.evidence: The electrons in the highest-numbered shell, plus any electrons in the last unfilled subshell, are called valence electrons
